questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I knew I wanted to stay in Europe because of the covid situation. I decided on Norway because I like the language, the nature and would like to explore more of the country. I was also important to me that the university I chose offered relevant courses for my study.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I has been an amazing experience, and I would recommend every student to go abroad.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
It took some time to orientate myself in the many different universities course catalogs. 
But other than that it was fine.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult to know which faculty I belonged to and also who I should contact to get the signature for the learning agreement. But in the end, it all worked out.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: If you go to Bergen I would really recommend you to find housing through the organization "sammen". And also to live at Fantoft student housing. Here we live over 500 students together. It has been such a big and important part of my stay here. I lived in a shred room with one girl and we shared a kitchen with 16 people. It sounds like a mess, but we have become a small family, and I wouldn't have wanted it in a different way.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I think off-campus is fine :) Especially if you live at Fantoft, because that feels like a huge university campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If you stay in Bergen --> Live at fantoft!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Bergen university has a very good course catalog and the application process is pretty straight forward.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Find the courses for you in the course catalog, apply for it on time and wait for an answer.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I allayed for two and i got them. So I am very pleased.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to check and know all deadlines. There are a lot of deadlines when appling for exchange. So be sure to write them down and not miss them.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level in Norway has been the same as in Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: One of my courses (Web design) at UIB has really surprised me in the best way. It has been very interesting and a more interactive and hands-on way of learning than I am used to, which I really enjoyed.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
DIKULT105 WEB DESIGN I
DIKULT203 ELECTRONIC LITERATURE

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you are a beginner and you are interested in learning to code websites, I would really recommend the WEB DESIGN I course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not so unexpected but if you want to also explore the country and do some trips, you might want to save some money for that.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and alcohol are very expensive in Norway, so take that into account.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Sammen is a student organisation in Bergen which offers a lot of great social things for students.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I join the sammen gym membership and some of the social things they planned like ice skating.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go hike the seven mountains. It is a must while being in Bergen.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hiking, exploring the city of Bergen, exploring the nightlife (Ricks, Heidis beer bar), go on trips. I went on a glacier tour at Folge fonna glacier. Was so amazing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Norway and Denmark are pretty close in culture, so very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I lived at Fantoft student housing where you will meet a lot of exchange students, so i did not get to meet so many norwegians. For me that wa okay because it was nice to spent this experience with other exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing :)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The hikinh culture they have here in Norway, and that there fell snow in December!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Live at Fantoft where you will meet so many exchange students
- Say yes to everything! ¨
- Explore more of the country than just Bergen while you are here.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is a very good university.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The amazing people I have met.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Learning how to code hahah. I studied web design. It was challenging but so rewarding in the end.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: If you have the possibility to go on exchange! Go for it!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
